# CTF writeup generator: standardized submission-style solution reports

Curated by Skill Harbor — @ljagiello's CTF writeup generator: after solving a challenge, document it as a single standardized submission-style writeup. Step 1, gather — collect challenge metadata, solution artifacts and the timeline from the session and challenge files (with find/grep hints to scan the workspace for solve scripts and flag formats). Step 2, generate — produce one complete writeup with metadata frontmatter (title, event, date, category, difficulty, points, flag format, author), 1–3 short solution steps built around a single complete solve script (challenge data in, flag printed out — no partial snippets), and a flag block. Includes a best-practices checklist (complete metadata, reproducible steps, runnable code, no real credentials or API keys, concise length, tool versions noted, proper attribution) and quality guidelines (front-load the main path, explain terminal output instead of dumping it, redact flags only if asked). Honest caveats: requires a filesystem-based agent (Claude Code or similar) with bash and Python 3; designed for documenting solved challenges — this is a reporting skill, not a solving one. MIT licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
